posts.title: PHP2Shell: 2 critical flaws, 1 urgent patch
bullets: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 affect PHP request handling. Both score 9.2 under CVSS 4.0.
Unauthenticated attackers may achieve remote code execution on exposed vulnerable PHP systems.
Fixed PHP releases: 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Check vendor backports for packaged versions.
posts.takeaway: Find exposed PHP systems, apply vendor fixes, restart services and verify versions.
posts.caption:
🚨 PHP2Shell: two critical PHP request-handling vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, were disclosed on 21 October 2026. They can enable unauthenticated remote code execution on vulnerable systems. Prioritize internet-facing PHP deployments and apply the relevant upstream or distribution security updates. Verify the running service after patching.

Sources: Ubuntu Security (21 Oct 2026), NHS England CSOC (21 Oct 2026).

#PHP2Shell #PHP #CVE #CyberSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement #TheCyberIntellect
posts.voiceover: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities are raising urgent questions for security teams. Vulnerable, exposed services may allow attackers to run code remotely. First, identify where PHP is running, especially on internet-facing systems. Next, check the PHP and distribution security advisories and apply the appropriate fix. Restart affected services, verify the running version, and confirm the vulnerability is closed. Patching is only complete when you validate the result.

posts.title: Can a web page hijack your AI agent?
bullets: An agent reads a web page or support ticket. Hidden text tells it to ignore its original task.
If the agent trusts those instructions, it might misuse connected tools or expose sensitive data.
OWASP calls this prompt injection. The 2026 guidance also highlights excessive agency and tool misuse.
posts.takeaway: Treat retrieved text as data. Limit tool permissions and require approval for risky actions.
posts.caption:
🤖 Your AI agent may be helpful. But can it tell trusted instructions from attacker-controlled web content?

Prompt injection happens when malicious instructions arrive through untrusted input, such as a page, document, ticket or tool result. A connected agent with broad permissions can turn a bad instruction into a real-world action. Use least-privilege tools, approval gates and strong audit logs.

Source: OWASP GenAI Security Project, 2026 Top 10 and Prompt Injection guidance.

#AISecurity #PromptInjection #AgenticAI #OWASP #CyberSecurity #TheCyberIntellect
posts.voiceover: Imagine your AI assistant reading a web page to answer a question. Hidden in that page is an instruction telling the agent to ignore the user and misuse its tools. That's prompt injection: untrusted content pretending to be an instruction. The defense is to treat retrieved text as data, limit tool permissions, require approval for sensitive actions, and keep useful audit logs. Never let a web page become your agent's boss.
